2_motivation:
s2_beyond_copy-B1's M1 measured that the champion `mf_fno_transfer_film` is **LF-blind at
inference** — `lf_at_inference = FALSE` on 5/5 datasets x 3/3 seeds,
`n_field_shaped_inputs_at_eval = 0`, "the only tensor entering the network at eval is the
`[16, cond_dim]` condition vector" (verified independently in
`factory_mffp/models/mf_fno_transfer_film/model.py::FNO2d.forward`, which lifts the coordinate
grid only). That makes the literal form of H2 untestable: a local operator needs a field, and
the champion has none. The only field available at test time is the interpolated LF field, so
the concrete s6 question is whether a **local operator acting on the real LF field** adds value
that the champion's global spectral generator cannot. The websearcher's verdict licenses exactly
this and only this: **D3 — "local corrector consuming the real interpolated LF field at test
time, with an identity-to-copy-LF construction (zero-init gate => at init the model IS copy-LF)"
— `preempted-but-MF-composition-open`**, open because "A no-harm floor **defined by a real
coarse PDE solve** (= round success criterion 2, skill < 1), plus the champion's blind spot that
it never sees LF at inference"; stream boundary respected — "`s2_beyond_copy`-B1 D2 already owns
'identity-to-LF'; **s6 owns only 'the corrector is LOCAL'**". The scouting websearch reached the
same class independently (C1, its rank-1 open composition) and sharpens the open surface to "a
**field-valued per-pixel/per-band trust gate** over the interpolated LF field inside a neural
operator, parameterized so the scored copy-LF reference is exactly recoverable and is the
initialization". One variant additionally carries D2 — "**preempted-but-MF-composition-open** ...
It also carries a *published opposing prediction* (F-Adapter says capacity belongs in LOW bands)
— a genuine pre-registered falsification risk". **No mechanism novelty is claimed**: parallel
local kernels in an FNO are peer-reviewed prior art (NO-LIDK ICML 2024; U-FNO; LOGLO-FNO), and
learned coarse-grid correction is standard (Kochkov 2021). The mentor's FNO->CNN two-stage
hybrid and iFNO **were trained off-repo with poor results reported ("not going well"); the code
and numbers are unavailable**, so no claim here rests on their absence — instead this design
differs from the plausible naive recipe on three stated axes: it **consumes the given LF field**
instead of predicting it (deleting the documented exposure-bias failure,
https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.02661), it is **zero-init and gated so copy-LF is exactly
recoverable**, and the local module is **capacity-constrained** (and, in variant 3, the *only*
HF-trained parameter set). Fact correction carried into the card: `n_train_hf = 400` on all five
beyond-copy datasets (s2-B1 part 5); **N_hf = 5 applies to `ifc_poisson` only**, so the
literature's "free-form refiner overfits at N=5" argument binds with full force only on the
ifc_poisson leg — which this card makes a no-op fallback.
3_description:
New family `models_r1/s6_local_lf_corrector`, one substrate, five env-selected variants.
Prediction on any dataset whose **test** split ships an LF fidelity (all five beyond-copy
datasets and all three guard datasets — verified on disk):
```
LF_up = interp(field_by_fid[max(lf_fids)] -> 256-capped working grid)   # == copy-LF construction
Delta = C_theta(LF_up, coords, FiLM(X))          # LOCAL: depthwise KxK ConvNeXt-lite stack
y_hat = LF_up + G (*) Delta                      # G = trust gate, EXACTLY 0 at init
```
- `C_theta`: depth 4, width 32, depthwise K=7 + pointwise, GroupNorm, per-block FiLM(X),
  **final 1x1 zero-init** => `Delta ≡ 0` at init. Receptive field ~25 cells.
- `G`: zero at init in every variant; its scalar component is finally selected on a held-out
  slice of the HF train split by least-squares projection + line search **whose candidate set
  contains 0** (construction reused from the in-round sibling `fno_transolver_seq`; cited, not
  claimed as novel).
- Target: `R = Y_hf - LF_up` on the HF train split.
- `max(lf_fids)` is mandatory: `eval/panel_data.py::copylf_prediction` uses the HIGHEST LF
  fidelity, while the champion's `smoke_eval.py` pretrains on `min(lf_fids)`.
- **Fallback**: `ifc_poisson`'s test split ships only `fidelity_64` (verified on disk), so there
  the family runs the champion path verbatim (LF-pretrain -> HF-finetune, X-only FiLM-FNO).
  Pre-registered **no-op leg**; no claim is made on ifc_poisson.
- **Builder tripwires**: (i) LF tensor must come from an LF fidelity array whose native grid is
  strictly coarser than HF (never a downsampled HF field); (ii) no HF *test* field may enter the
  prediction path; (iii) the identity path's nRMSE must match `eval/copylf_baselines.json` up to
  the interpolation-kernel difference (`scipy.zoom order=1` vs `F.interpolate bilinear`), delta
  recorded in `build_notes`; (iv) attempt a re-fetch of the unresolved prior-art threat
  **AGMF-Net** (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S002980182502997X, HTTP 403
  for both websearchers) and record the outcome.

**Ranked variants (ADR 0007)** — one card, one worktree, one SLURM chain:

| rank | `S6_VARIANT` | recipe delta | rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `local_pixel_gate` | `g(x) = sigmoid(h(x) + b0)` with hard-zero offset so `g ≡ 0` at init | the scout's rank-1 open composition (field-valued trust gate); local corrector + local gate = maximal s6 ownership |
| 2 | `local_scalar_gate` | one scalar gate, held-out selected | clean control for rank 1: does spatial trust structure beat one number? simplest, most robust |
| 3 | `lf_frozen_adapter` | spectral encoder trained on **LF only**, then FROZEN; the **only** HF-trained params are the zero-init local adapter + gate | the D2 arm; tests F-Adapter's published opposing prediction (scarce capacity belongs in LOW bands) |
| 4 | `local_band_gate` | 4 per-band scalar gates, edges `k_nyq * [0, 1/8, 1/4, 1/2, 1]` (s2-B1 convention), all init 0 | makes the low-band no-harm claim hard and per-band auditable |
| 5 | `pointwise_ctrl` | `S6_KERNEL=1` (receptive field = 1 cell) | isolates locality-as-spatial-kernel from pure pointwise recalibration — H2's real content given s2-B1 M5a amplitude findings |

**Screening plan**: ONE contract-tier job (`--epochs 2 --seed 0`), all five variants, on
`--datasets panel` **and** `--datasets guard` (the card will claim a panel win, so §2.3 requires
the guard set). Reserve 01:00:00 (s2-B1 precedent: 5 datasets, 46 s on H100).
*Primary function of the screen is the **no-harm assertion**, not ranking*: every variant must
score `skill <= 1.02` on each of the five beyond-copy datasets at 2 epochs; a violation means the
identity construction is broken (ALGO). With a gate whose search set contains 0, all variants are
expected to sit at ~1.000 and be indistinguishable on the scored metric at 2 epochs.
**Discard rule**: drop only on (i) crash/NaN, (ii) no-harm violation, (iii) 5-dataset contract
geomean > 2x the best variant's. Close calls are NOT discarded (ADR 0007).
**Promotion rule (fixed before submit, no post-hoc switching)**: among survivors promote the
highest mean held-out residual-explained fraction `rho = 1 - ||R - G*Delta||^2/||R||^2` over the
five beyond-copy datasets, *provided* it beats the runner-up by > 0.05 absolute; otherwise
promote by rank order 1->2->3->4->5. `rho` is a plumbing/gross-ordering signal recorded in
`build_notes` only and is never quoted as evidence in parts 5-7 (ADR 0007 guardrail). If no
variant survives, the card is ALGO-broken -> debugger.
**Promoted run**: 200 epochs, seed 0, `--datasets panel`; reserve 06:00:00
(`state/timing_ledger.json`: champion 200-epoch panel legs sum to ~186 min; the corrector stage
adds to that).

**Pre-registered gaming hazard (coordinator direction)**: with an identity-init gate,
`skill <= 1.0` is reachable **at initialization**, so **raw skill is explicitly NOT this card's
win condition**. The readout is the *trained gate's contribution*, written as sidecar
diagnostics computed through `eval/nrmse.py` on the family's own predictions (no new scored
metric; §2.1 untouched): `skill_id` (the `G ≡ 0` path — deterministic, zero seed variance),
`contribution_d = skill_id - skill_trained`, the per-band contribution profile
`||e_b(trained)||^2 / ||e_b(identity)||^2` on the s2-B1 band grid, and the gate statistics
(selected scalar / mean and percentiles of `g(x)` / fraction of pixels with `g > 0.01`).
**A gate that collapses to zero is a FINDING (learned fusion adds nothing on top of the real
coarse solve), not a failure.**

5_cross_stream_sanity.physical_plausibility: All four datasets where the corrector fires are nested factor-2 ladders (LF 128^2 -> HF 256^2, pfc 64^2 -> 128^2), where the residual R = Y_hf - LF_up is dominated by the leading discretization/interpolation-truncation term, a LOCAL differential functional of the LF field. Learning it is machine-learned defect correction / Richardson extrapolation, which is expected to remove most of the leading term and leave the next order: allen_cahn residual-of-residual 0.0013/0.01615 = 8.1%, pfc 3.0%, fisher_kpp 9.5%. Where the LF solve is NOT in that asymptotic regime (helmholtz, ratio 4, oscillatory) the mechanism has nothing to exploit and the gate correctly shut off. The mechanism's on/off pattern tracks the physics, which is the strongest single argument that this is real.

An ORACLE per-pixel gate fitted on the test set itself buys 4.1% (pfc), 1.2% (allen_cahn), 0.6% (fisher_kpp) and is HARMFUL on cahn_hilliard (0.0481634 vs 0.0410771, +17%). The ACHIEVABLE version (fitted on the held-out val slice) is worse than g==1 on 3 of 4 (allen_cahn 0.0013317, fisher_kpp 0.0060251, cahn_hilliard 0.0442227). Correlation between the learned gate's pixel map and the oracle map is 0.10-0.22 on the four winners.

An oracle per-sample scalar gate on the same trained Delta gives pfc 0.0010441 (-22.8% vs g==1) and helmholtz 0.1623286 vs copy-LF 0.3294501 (-50.7%, i.e. skill 0.49 on the one dataset the card reports as a no-op), against <= 4.1% for the oracle per-pixel map. On helmholtz with alpha forced to 1, a val-fitted per-pixel gate gets 0.5601 - better than 1.4743 (g==1) but still worse than copy-LF's 0.3295; only per-sample selection helps there.

F4 (turn 1) THE STAGED PROTOCOL MAKES g == 1 THE CORRECT ANSWER, NOT A FAILED ONE. Uniform-gate landscape J(c) = mean((c*Delta - R)^2): argmin c = 1.0 on the fit, held-out val AND test splits simultaneously on all four winners, and J(0) = ||R||^2 is the landscape MAXIMUM, so from g == 0 the stage-2 gradient pushes g up at every pixel. The corrector shows no generalization gap on three winners (relative error ||R-Delta||/||R|| fit/val/test: pfc 0.0248/0.0237/0.0234, allen_cahn 0.0773/0.0955/0.0854, fisher_kpp 0.0941/0.1004/0.0990), so there is no trust signal to represent.

Stage 2 trains the pixel gate on the SAME fit_idx that stage 1 fitted Delta on, so it cannot see that gap and still saturates near 1 (g_mean 0.9970); stage 3 selects the scalar on val_idx and chose alpha = 0. All demonstrated trust behaviour therefore comes from the OUT-OF-SAMPLE scalar, and the card's per-pixel-trust mechanism is unsupported.

interpretation: M1 MECHANISM VERDICT (high confidence, directly measured). The card's mechanism is NOT 'per-pixel trust routing over the LF field'. It is (i) base = the real coarse solve, (ii) a LOCAL additive corrector that learns the nested ladder's leading truncation defect - a compact, nearly shift-invariant, nearly sample-independent LINEAR operator of the LF field, i.e. machine-learned Richardson-style defect correction - and (iii) a HELD-OUT SCALAR on/off switch that disables the whole correction where (ii) does not hold. The pixel gate contributes <= 0.63% (F1) and even an oracle pixel map contributes <= 4.1% (F2); most of what the ConvNeXt learns is reproduced, and on 3 of 4 datasets beaten, by a closed-form filter (F6).

M2 WHY THE GATE IS A NO-OP (high confidence). Two independent reasons, and only the second is a protocol defect: (a) per-pixel trust has essentially no headroom on these datasets (F2), and (b) stage 2 optimises the gate on the same fit_idx that stage 1 fitted Delta on, so it is blind to generalization error by construction; its loss is minimised at g == 1 on every split where the corrector generalizes (F4) and it still saturates at ~1 on the one dataset where it should not (F5). The staged protocol therefore CANNOT test the per-pixel-trust hypothesis as posed - a gate head trained on the held-out slice (corrector frozen, stage 2 moved AFTER the split) is the one-line change that would.

M3 WHY THE PRE-REGISTRATION OVERSHOT AND INVERTED (high confidence). The card forecast a deterministic mechanism with a statistical statistic. LF<->HF band coherence measures shared randomness; what governs a defect corrector is whether R is a fixed operator of LF, measured by the held-out rho of an LF->R fit - which orders the panel perfectly including the helmholtz shut-off (F14) and is training-free. pfc is simultaneously the panel's most LSI-learnable dataset and its least band-coherent one, which is exactly how the predicted-null dataset delivered the largest effect.

M4 WHAT LIMITS THE MECHANISM (high confidence). Three joint conditions: nested refinement in the coarse solve's ASYMPTOTIC regime (so its error is the leading truncation term), STATIONARITY of that error across samples (one operator for all), and LOCALITY (compact stencil). helmholtz violates the first two - ratio 4 with LF 24^2 on an oscillatory problem, so the coarse solve is not converged and its error is a sample-dependent dispersion/phase error: rho_fit only 0.484 (it cannot even fit in-sample) and rho_val -43.9. It is a REGIME boundary, not a refinement-ratio boundary; ratio 4 with a resolved coarse solve should still work. cahn_hilliard is the marginal case on stationarity (F13).

M5 CAHN_HILLIARD IS THE s3_warp HANDOFF (hypothesis, well supported). Its low band (99.7% of the error energy) barely moves for either arm (0.919 NN / 0.918 LSI), its trained rho collapses out of sample (0.883 -> 0.083), 51% of samples get worse in band 2, and 4% get worse overall - i.e. the remaining error is not interface-truncation and is not fixed by a better local additive filter. A displacement/alignment mechanism is the live hypothesis, which is s3_warp's territory.

M6 THE CLASS-B RETIREMENT IS CONFIRMED AND SHARPENED (high confidence). s2-B1 labelled allen_cahn and fisher_kpp 'residual-unlearnable at N=400' from a global-signature kNN (L5 skill 1.042 / 1.062). Both are now STRONG defect-correction datasets (held-out rho 0.997 / 0.984; skill 0.056 / 0.123 from a filter with no free nonlinear parameters). The distinction is estimator-class: a whole-field lookup asks 'which training FIELD resembles this one', a defect operator asks 'what does a fixed local functional of this field predict' - and on nested ladders the second question has a deterministic answer. s2-B1's F13 mid-band locality on fisher_kpp is reproduced (copy-LF band shares [0.099,0.653,0.232,0.016]) and is exactly where the NN beats the linear filter 2.5x (band-1 contribution 0.0032 vs 0.0081), consistent with fisher-KPP's local nonlinearity u(1-u) being the one genuinely nonlinear defect on the panel.

M7 WHAT THE 0.2346 GEOMEAN IS AND IS NOT (high confidence). It is a real, seam-checked win over copy-LF on 4 of 5 beyond-copy datasets, and turn 3 shows a filter with ZERO trained parameters would score even better on 3 of them (panel-relevant skills 0.0139 / 0.0564 / 0.4439 / 0.1231) - so the result is robust to the whole neural-network question. But that also bounds its architectural content: it is not evidence that a local ConvNeXt branch, FiLM conditioning, per-pixel trust, or 200 epochs of training were necessary. The scientific content is the DEFECT-CORRECTION TARGET plus the held-out switch, not the operator class.
surprises: A zero-parameter closed-form filter beats the round's best trained model on 3 of the 4 datasets it wins on (pfc 2.19x, allen_cahn 1.56x, cahn_hilliard 1.07x). The 200-epoch, 72k-parameter, FiLM-conditioned ConvNeXt is a worse defect corrector than one least-squares transfer function - the honest headline for this composition is the target, not the network.

The beyond-LF-Nyquist gain that part 5 flagged as 'the most likely place for an artifact to hide' is real and is stronger than measured: a LINEAR filter reduces pfc's band-3 (k 32-64) error energy to 5.0e-12 of copy-LF's. Bilinear upsampling leaves deterministic spectral replicas that a fixed filter inverts.

An oracle per-pixel trust gate makes cahn_hilliard WORSE (+17%): a single pixel map shared across samples cannot describe a dataset whose sample-to-sample error spread is 4.4x its mean. Per-pixel trust was not merely unlearned, it was the wrong granularity.

helmholtz, the card's report-only no-op, has the panel's largest available per-sample trust headroom: an oracle per-sample scalar on the SAME trained corrector scores 0.1623 vs copy-LF's 0.3295 (skill 0.49). The dataset where the mechanism shut itself off is the dataset where per-sample routing would pay most, which lines up with s2-B1 F10 (3% of helmholtz samples carry 50% of copy-LF's error).

Up to 81% of the trained corrector's remaining squared error sits within 12 cells of the domain boundary on periodic datasets, while the implicitly-periodic closed-form filter shows no such excess - the reviewer's zero-padding carry-forward is not a small correction, it is the largest identified headroom item on this family.
